quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue of NT$1832 hundred million, a record single quarter, up 48% YoY and 15% QoQ, with AI data-center demand the main growth driver (power electronics revenue +50%, led by power supplies and liquid-cooling components; data-center infrastructure solutions including liquid cooling also grew fast). Gross margin 35.6% (best quarter ever except Q1, gross profit +48% YoY); operating income a record NT$306 hundred million at a 16.7% operating margin, +64% YoY; net income to parent about NT$251 hundred million, +80% YoY and +22% QoQ; EPS a record NT$9.68; EBITDA a record NT$441 hundred million at a 24% margin. H1: revenue NT$3426 hundred million +41% YoY, operating profit +80%, net income about NT$457 hundred million (up nearly 90%), EPS NT$17.59 (+89%) - already above any prior full year. Data-center-related business now contributes more than half of group revenue.

quarterly_data.signal: H2 is expected to be better than H1, with Q3 seasonally the strongest quarter; margins are seen holding around current levels - management cautions against expecting further margin expansion even as large CSP customers ramp, and says needed price increases for higher raw-material costs will be passed on with a timing lag. AI-related products will exceed 25% of group revenue this year (versus the roughly 20% target given earlier); the group grew 31% last year and this year should be higher. Hyperscaler capex keeps rising - the majors indicated this year's capex goes higher still and 2027 should increase again - so the AI data-center build-out is not expected to stop near term, though construction delays, key-component issues and US public sentiment (strong local opposition to data centers; New York state paused fifty-mega-scale projects by executive order) are watch items. Mobility (EV) stays weak this year with contained losses, while the BA unit returns to normal shipments in H2 after memory-sourcing design changes.
quarterly_data.figure: AI-related products above 25% of revenue this year (prior target about 20%); group revenue +31% last year with higher growth expected this year

quarterly_data.signal: HVDC ramp: plus/minus 400V and 800V systems start mass production in Q3 2026, but Q4 shipments and full-year volume stay limited - larger volume comes next year. The plus/minus 400V architecture is being pushed more aggressively and ships more this year; 800V is driven mainly by NVIDIA and depends on when data-center operators adopt that power architecture - NVIDIA's Blackwell shipments are still much larger than Rubin, and part of the Rubin lineup can still run on low voltage. On the 110kW power shelf and other new product cycles Delta believes its market share remains high because it engages customers earliest, and the fast generational churn of AI power architecture favors its engineering resources; it declined to quantify share for the Rubin-linked 110kW PSU but asserts market leadership. A solid-state transformer (an energy gateway, not a one-for-one transformer replacement) has its first trial customers in smaller data centers, and a first small fuel-cell line starts by year-end with the first volume line planned next year, with units at Taipower and another test site performing well.
quarterly_data.figure: HVDC plus/minus 400V and 800V mass production from Q3, limited volume this year, ramp next year; 110kW power shelf share seen high

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid cooling keeps scaling: liquid-cooling products were about 10% of group revenue last year and will exceed 12% this year (an analyst cited about US$1.6 billion of Liquid-to-Air contribution last year). Management expects Liquid-to-Air to persist considerably longer than the market's assumption that Liquid-to-Liquid fully takes over around 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: liquid cooling about 10% of revenue last year, above 12% this year; Liquid-to-Air about US$1.6B contribution last year

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity is being pre-built for multi-year AI and energy demand: Thailand plant 1 is being rebuilt with several times its old capacity and three more Thai plants finish this year and next; China, Taiwan and the US are all expanding, a US building was bought for R&D, and one more overseas operations site is under negotiation. H1 capex was NT$275 hundred million and H2 will exceed NT$400 hundred million - roughly NT$700 hundred million for the year versus NT$466 hundred million last year; if next year's growth stays high, capex stays at that level or higher. Large customers are already booking next year's volumes and the requested amounts are big; beyond AI, the next demand leg is energy infrastructure/microgrid (grid, self-generation, energy storage), where single projects run to several hundred million dollars. From April this year all AI-related equipment is depreciated over 3 years (previously up to 5) as a conservative policy.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 capex NT$275 hundred million, H2 above NT$400 hundred million, about NT$700 hundred million full year vs NT$466 hundred million last year

quarterly_data.signal: Component supply is tight across the board: lead times are stretching and MOSFETs in particular are short, though Delta's purchasing scale and supplier relationships keep demand largely fulfilled. Memory was the hardest hit - one business unit could not secure memory volumes at workable prices, so it switched designs to second sources and expects H2 shipments to normalize and catch up the backlog without a loss. Management does not expect power semiconductors to repeat memory's shortage dynamics - the two situations differ a lot - but notes power-semi supply is cyclical because capacity investment takes long. On wide-bandgap devices (silicon carbide, gallium nitride) Delta works early and closely with the most important suppliers, keeps talking with them continuously and gets early access to new products, but will not disclose any agreements; it is also broadening its supply chain, including Taiwanese supplier options. Supplier price increases will be negotiated and passed to customers where the business model allows, with a timing lag.
